questions.stem: Tea-drinking started in ____.

context.text: Tea and coffee are two of the most popular drinks in the world. However, these drinks are used differently in different cultures.

Tea-drinking started in China over 4,000 years ago. Tea is made from leaves. These days, some people drink tea to relieve (缓解) stress or lose weight. However, most people in tea-drinking countries think of tea as more than just a drink. In fact, tea-drinking in some countries is a part of the culture. In Turkey, tea is always there when people meet. Whether in someone’s home or a company, tea is always offered as a way of welcome. In the U.K., afternoon tea is common in homes and offices. Tea and other dishes are served at tea time. It is a way of relaxing with friends or co-workers.

Coffee came just over 1,000 years ago, much later than tea. Coffee is made from coffee beans. Something in the beans makes a person feel active. Most people do not drink coffee to relax. Instead, they drink coffee to get going. Many people drink coffee in the morning to help them stay awake. Others also drink coffee during short breaks in the afternoon to keep going through the working days. Some people may visit coffee shops just to meet and talk with friends. However, many people in coffee shops drink coffee while working on their computers.
Is tea or coffee popular in your country? Which one do you like to drink more?

questions.stem: How long did Mark Twain stay in Maine?

context.text: Mark Twain was a famous American writer. He loved writing, hunting and fishing very much. Once he went to Maine on vacation and spent three happy weeks there.

When he decided to get back, Mark Twain went to the station with his baggage (行李). After putting it on the train, he sat in a comfortable seat. He thought it would be impolite to say nothing at that moment, so he said good morning to the man first and began to chat with him. They talked about the weather and then Maine. The man said, “We have some beautiful woods in Maine, and I guess you have been there, haven’t you?”

“Yes, I have,” answered Mark Twain, “I have just spent three pleasant weeks there, and I’d like to tell you something: Though fishing isn’t allowed in Maine this season, I’ve got two hundred pounds of beautiful fish. I like eating fish, so I put them on ice to take them home. May I know something about you, sir?”
The man looked at Mark Twain for several seconds and answered, “I’m a policeman. My job is to catch people who hunt and fish during the wrong season. And what do you do?”
Mark Twain answered, “Well, sir, I’m the man who tells the biggest lie in America.”

questions.stem: We can learn from the text that not getting enough sleep might cause people to ____.

context.text: After a day of work and play, the body needs rest. Enough sleep is necessary for good health. In sleep, the body recovers from the activities of the previous day. The rest that you get while sleeping enables your body to prepare itself for the next day.

There are four levels of sleep, each being a little deeper than the one before. As you sleep, your muscles relax little by little. Your heart beats more slowly, and your brain slows down. After you reach the fourth level, your body shifts back and forth from one level of sleep to another.

Although your mind slows down, from time to time you will dream. Scientists who study sleep say that when dreaming occurs, your eyeballs begin to move more quickly (although your eyelids are closed). This stage of sleep is called REM, which stands for Rapid Eye Movement.

If you have trouble falling asleep, some people recommend that you breathe deeply. Other people believe that drinking warm milk will help make you drowsy. There is also an old suggestion that counting sheep will help you fall asleep.
